about: A Zork I style opening. You enter the white house through the window, take the lantern and sword, and go down the trap door to the cellar. A troll guards the Troll Room, and beyond it the world stops at unfinished passages.

done.why: Every route below the house ended in an unfinished passage. The trap door had barred behind me, so I had no way back up. I found no treasure and nothing else to do.

ending.what: No ending. The explorable area stops at the Troll Room and the cellar crawlway.

moments.note: I tried to take the lantern and sword in one command. It said 'You can't see any such thing', yet 'turn on lantern' then worked.
The session reset. 'inventory' returned 'Arrive first.' and I had to arrive again and replay.
The sword's blue glow warned me about the troll, and I killed it in two blows.
The east passage was blocked by a joke note from 'The Management' saying the passage is unfinished.

wished: I wanted to find treasure and bring it to the trophy case.
I wanted to go on past the troll into the rest of the underground.
I wanted to be able to go back up the trap door.

lines.line: Your sword has begun to glow very brightly.
lines.why: It warned me about the troll before I could see it.

lines.line: The passage to the east has not been finished. Someone has left a pick leaning against the rock, and a note: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: It explained that the world stops here, and it did so with some humour.

fun.why: The opening was familiar and fun, and the troll fight was satisfying. Then it ran out.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal, but nothing further to pursue once the troll was dead.

difficulty.why: I had a lantern and a sword, and the troll died in two blows.

interestingness.why: It was a faithful opening, and the dead-end notes were clever. There was little to discover.

prose.why: The room descriptions are clean and match the original, and the dead-end notes are funny.
